szb_001: You can recognise it by its massive trunk, over six metres round, standing alone where the old floodplain wood has been cleared. It stands on the riverside promenade near the Traklsteg footbridge.
szb_002: You can recognise it by its single, thick stem standing over the yard of the Erentrudishof farm shop. It stands on the organic farm's grounds, run by Stift Nonnberg convent at Morzg.
szb_003: You can recognise it by its position right at the woodland edge, a short walk from the tram stop toward Birkensiedlung. It stands on the southern edge of Morzg, on public ground.
szb_004: You can recognise it as the lime tree growing roadside on Körblleitengasse, between Kleßheimer Allee and Norbert-Brüll-Straße. It stands on this residential lane in Maxglan.
szb_006: You can recognise it by its trunk, splitting into several strong branches about five metres up, with ivy climbed most of the way up it. It stands on the pavement of Steinbruchstraße in Riedenburg.
szb_009: You can recognise it by its trunk standing alone in the open courtyard of the Fordhof housing estate, off Rainerstraße; the black pine grows about 35 metres away in the same courtyard.
